utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I see the witness is here. Let him make the declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Sachdeva, you're up.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. President, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Good morning, Witness.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Just to let you know that your request for -- or our request on your behalf for protection was granted and your image will be distorted so that the public will not see your face. Can you start by telling the Court your full name, date and plays of birth, please.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: My name is Mirza Sabljica. I was born on the 26th of February, 1966 in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mr. President, may I lead the witness through some of his personal details.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mr. Sabljica, it's correct that you obtained a degree in mechanical engineering before the war; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: Yes. I graduated from the Faculty of Mechanical Engineering in Sarajevo on the 10th of October, 1991.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: The interpreter didn't hear the year very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Can you repeat the year again, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Did you join the CSB in June 1993?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And what was your job description at the CSB?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: I was hired as an expert for ballistics and mechanical traces.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Before you were hired in that position, did you undergo any training?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: You mean before I was admitted to the police force or to that position?

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Before or upon being admitted to the police force for that job.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: Before that, I was a member of the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina from the beginning of the war until June 1993; and when I transferred to the police, I had intensive training on the job for the -- for the profession in which I continued later.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And being an expert from June 1993 for ballistics and mechanical traces, what did that job entail precisely?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: In addition to examining the traces made by use of fire-arms and the use of various tools on various types of locks, our job was to work on cases of shelling of civilian targets in the city of Sarajevo, to examine traces created by the use of various types of artillery pieces, determine the direction from which projectiles were fired and to determine the type of projectile. That is brief my job description for the period I worked in the police.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: You said "our job." Did you work with other people in this particular department for ballistics and mechanical traces?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: Certainly. Since I was the most junior member of that team, I had the benefit of the knowledge and experience of my more experienced colleague, my senior colleagues who had been on the force for a long time and who were experts in ballistics and mechanical traces. Unfortunately, I must say that all three of them are no who are no longer alive.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: You said you worked on cases of shelling of civilian targets in the city of Sarajevo. Can you be more specific. Did you work on cases of mortar explosions in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: I can say that in 90 per cent of cases I dealt with mortar projectiles, and we exclusively went out to perform on-site investigations when civilian targets were involved.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: When you went on site to conduct your investigations, was it your job to determine the direction of fire from evidence that you may see on the ground?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: Yes, the direction of fire, trajectory, and the type of projectile. We never discussed the location.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And with respect to mortars, what was it that assisted you to determine the direction of fire when you went to an on-site investigation?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: The traces you find on the spot after a shell hits are useful. We used a special method, the same one used by members of the UNPROFOR and other ballistic experts, and I can explain that method if you wish me.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: I'm going to ask to you explain that with the assistance of photographs in a moment. Let me ask you: From the period that you joined the CSB in 1993 to the end of the conflict in December 1995, roughly, how many mortar incidents involving civilians did you investigate?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: I can say with certainty there were more than 50 cases, and let me emphasise, again, that we went out to perform on-site investigations only when there were human losses. We didn't go out when there were only casualties, wounded, or injured people. There were over 50 such cases involving death.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And when you went out on the scene, you said that you would look at -- you said that you would look at traces that you would find on the spot. Traces from what exactly?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: Mechanical traces resulting from impact of projectiles and fragments and that would be contoured on an asphalt surface or some other surface.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: What is that analysis typically known as?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: We called it analysis of the central axis, and it's a very simple one.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And was this from the craters that were left on the asphalt, from mortar explosions?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, based on the appearance of the crater and traces resulting from the explosion of a projectile.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And this analysis that you conducted from the craters on the ground, would you say this was a complicated or a simple process?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: For laymen, it may appear complicated at the beginning, but basically it's a very simple process that is based on the basic principles of mathematics and geometry.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: When you came to a conclusion of a direction of fire from this crater analysis from this process, how accurate would you say you were?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: Normally, in our reports, we would indicate a margin of error that was plus/minus five per cent concerning the direction of the shell.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Was it ever the case in your work, and indeed the work of your colleagues, that upon seeing a crater on the ground that you could be mistaken in terms of direction of fire by some 40 or 50 degrees?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: Not as far as I know. That never happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mr. Sabljica --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: Excuse me. [Interpretation] Excuse me, Prosecutor. I have a question before we go any further. Witness, please, the question on your training, you graduate in mechanical engineering and you said that as far as -- that crater analysis is quite simple and the procedure is quite simple. So as a civilian engineer, when you were trained as a civilian mechanical engineer, did you study crater analysis or was it something that you were trained on separately? When I read your resume, I see that you're a mechanical engineer, and it also says that you are expert on mechanical traces and ballistics. So when did you get the training on ballistics and on crater analysis?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I received my training at the Security Services Centre; that is, on the police force, as soon as I began working there in June 1993. I under went intensive courses while working in the specific conditions of war. So that with the assistance of my senior colleagues who were high instructors, I acquired skills and improved my knowledge. But in order to be able to do that job as all, you have to have a background knowledge; a degree in mechanical engineering, for instance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fine. So in order to be able to understand the analysis and crater analysis, you need to have a good background, possibly in mechanical engineering. Is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. But did all police officers follow this training in crater analysis? All the other ones, were they also trained as their background in mechanical engineering, the more experienced ones who trained you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Two of them did have degrees in mechanical engineering. Another one was an electrical engineer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Are you saying then that some kind of a background in engineering, whether it be mechanical or electrical, is required?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, certainly, because basically the most important things are mechanics and mathematics.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: How long did your training last?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My intensive training was for eight and a half months.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: On completion of the training, were you awarded with a certificate or anything else to indicate that you had undergone that training?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Upon finishing that course, I got a certificate saying that I was an expert for ballistics and mechanical traces in the Security Services Centre in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: The certificate actually said that the training that you received qualified you as an expert for ballistics and mechanical traces; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, precisely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Sachdeva.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mr. Sabljica, just following on from questions from the Bench. You said earlier when I asked you about the specific process when you determine the direction of fire from a crater you said it was basically a simple process. Now, I want to ask you this: Do you have to have had a background or would you have had to have been a mechanical engineer to have and able to analyse a crater and come to a conclusion as to direction of fire? Is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: Yes. Basically, yes. You had to have some sort of background in engineering in order to be able to perform that job at all, to qualify under the requirements prescribed for that job.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Now I want to ask you: Did you testify for another case at the Tribunal before you have come here today?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: Yes. I think five years ago in the Galic case, I believe.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And when you testified for the Galic case, just very briefly, what was the subject of your evidence?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: I testified about three cases and three corresponding reports of our ballistic team; that is, Markale 1, humanitarian aid in Dobrinja, one case of shelling in Alipasino Polje.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And the Markale 1 incident and the humanitarian aid incident in Dobrinja, were they also shelling cases?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: Yes. Mortar projectiles were involved and a large number of deaths.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And for those cases, did you determine the direction of fire?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: Yes, certainly, like in any other case.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And you said that the mortar projectiles were involved in a large number of deaths. Were these deaths civilians or were they military personnel?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: I repeat: We only went out to perform on-site investigations where civilians had met their death.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: You mention that you conducted an investigation into an incident in Alipasino Polje. The casualties in that incident, what kind of casualties were they?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: That case involved children only.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Tapuskovic is on his feet.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would like to make a small objection to the question posed by Mr. Sachdeva because all these events, according to the information I received from the Prosecution a couple of days ago, all of these events fall beyond the period with which Mr. Milosevic is charged with. Alipasino Polje happened on the 24th of January, 1994, and the other case was on the 4th of February, 1994. So that is outside the scope of the indictment. I don't think, therefore, that these matters can be directly relevant to what this witness is supposed to testify about. He is supposed to testify about the cases that fall within the indictment of Mr. Dragomir Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Sachdeva.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mr. President, what I would say to learned counsel is, firstly, the Prosecution indictment states specifically that the accused inherited a campaign of shelling and sniping when he took over command of the SRK. Secondly, given the decision -- given Your Honour's decision with respect to the adjudicated facts and, of course, pending the request for certification on that decision, the Prosecution's position -- the Prosecution is therefore necessitated for the Prosecution to lead some evidence of crimes committed -- alleged crimes committed in that period prior to Dragomir Milosevic taking command, but when he was -- the Prosecution says Chief of Staff of the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps. And the material I'm asking the witness about is material that is closed to the Defence. I don't intend to tender any exhibits through this witness pertaining to those incidents, and in fact I'm finished with that subject.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: So tell us even more specifically why you're leading this evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: The reason I'm leading the evidence is because the evidence will eventually, we allege, go to the notice of the accused while he was Chief of Staff and prior to him taking over command, and, of course, the Prosecution's position is that there were -- there was a campaign already in place against civilians through shelling and sniping. And while Dragomir Milosevic was Chief of Staff, the Prosecution' submission would be that he must have known about these incidents. And in light of the adjudicated facts decision where, as I understand it, facts from the Appeals Chamber decision and the Trial Chamber decision concluding that there was shelling and sniping of civilians in the period prior to the accused's command, they have not been admitted as adjudicated facts, and therefore the Prosecution is leading this type of evidence, in a very, very brief fashion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: The Chamber will allow the evidence to be led for the reason stated by the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mr. Sabljica, I think we -- we stopped at your answer with respect to the incident, Alipasino Polje, that involved children, and I want to ask you about the Markale 1 incident. Do you remember how many people were killed in that incident?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: I think there were 69 dead and over 90 wounded.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Do you remember the date, roughly, of that incident?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: 4th or 5th February.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: You also mentioned an incident involving humanitarian aid in Dobrinja. Do you recall roughly how many people -- how many casualties there were in that incident?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: I think there were about six dead and wounded. I don't remember, really.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: What were these people doing in Dobrinja at the time?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: They were queueing for humanitarian aid.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Now, you -- we've just spoken about shelling. Did you also conduct investigations into sniping incidents?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: Certainly. That was an integral component of my job.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And while you were at the CSB, can you tell the Court roughly how many incidents involving sniping did you investigate?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: Certainly more than shelling incidents. I believe there were over 60 cases.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Now I'm going to show you a photograph, and I'm going to ask you more specific questions about the process that you take when analysing a crater.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mr. President, if I could ask for 65 ter 2112, and if we could move to the third photograph, please. Can it be enlarged?

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Witness, do you see a photograph on the screen?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Maybe it shouldn't be broadcast. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: What do you see there?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: I see a clear trace made by a mortar shell and some people standing around. One is there at the entrance to building number 26. There are also these three sticks that we used in order to graphically depict how we worked and what method we employed; that is, the method of the central axis in order to determine the direction of the projectile based on the trace it left on the surface.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Do you know which incident this is?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: I believe that this was the shelling of Kosevsko Brdo, Livanjska Street.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And were you involved in that investigation?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Do you remember the date of that incident?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: This was 13 years ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: If you can't remember, it's okay.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: No, I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And in that incident, do you recall how many shells landed on Livanjska Street?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: I believe that in this particular case there was only one shell.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And when you say "in this particular case," are you speaking with reference to this mortar -- the crater that you see in the photograph?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: Yes, that's the one I'm referring to.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And on this location, do you recall if there was another shell that landed?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: I remember that we conducted an on-site investigation on Livanjska Street where two more shells fell but not in front of building 26, but it was number 30 or something. But I also am not sure whether that was on the same day.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Okay. Now, in this photograph, just explain -- I want you to explain, first, how many sticks do we see here?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: You can see three sticks here.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And where the three sticks meet, what is that point?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: That's the centre of the explosion, or rather, the centre of the crater, and you can see the projectile stabiliser there in the centre.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And the two horizontal sticks, do you see the two horizontal sticks? What do they signify?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: In order for you to comprehend more fully this method, I think it would be useful if I can explain it in more detail, if you wish.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Please do.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: A mortar shell, when landing, its axis creates a angle with the surface which is normally less than 90 degrees. During contact with the surface and the explosion, there's a fragmentation of the shell that occurs, and the traces on the surface are visible and they spread at a longer distance from the centre of the explosion in the direction from which the shell had come. They create an irregular ellipsis in the shape of a fan, because from that direction the explosive impact is directed lower to the surface; whereas, on the opposite side, the impact of the shell grenades tend to go upwards, and therefore there are fewer traces on the surface than in the place indicating the direction of fire. In order to employ this method, you have to have approximately this arrangement or this picture that I explained which depicts how explosion occurred. These sticks actually indicate the hands of an angle by connecting the farthest traces from the direction of fire with the centre of the explosion, and then you draw a central axis on them, which at the same time indicates the direction from which the shell came. If you allow me, I can also say that usually these are more sharper angles, and this is a typical case here on Kosevsko Brdo, and you can see that there is in the shape of a letter T.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: I'm going to ask the court usher to hand you a pen to mark this photograph. You talked about the traces on the surface that are visible, and they spread at a longer distances from the centre of the explosion in the direction from which the shell had come. I want you to take a pen and mark those traces.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: These are the traces.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And you also said these sticks actually indicate the hands of an angle by connecting the farthest trace of the direction of fire to the centre of the explosion. Can you indicated where these farthest traces are?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: This one here and this one here, as can you see in the photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: So they correspond to the ends of horizontal sticks?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: Precisely so.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And the vertical stick coming from the -- from the centre of the explosion, what does that signify?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: It signifies that central axis, and it indicates the direction from which the shell came.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mr. President, I ask that this photograph is tendered into evidence -- admitted into evidence, sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We admit it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As P571, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: May I now ask for exhibit --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor, before we leave this picture, I would like you to ask the witness if he can testify to the kind of mortar we see here and also explain to us what he was saying about the tail-fin of the mortar. I understood him to say that the tail-fin was embedded in the crater, and I would be curious to know just why the tail-fin would remain there and not be thrown away by the explosion.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mr. Sabljica, did you hear that question. Firstly, you said that the tail-fin was embedded in the crater. Do you know why it remained there?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: Usually, due to an explosion, we often found the tail-fin embedded in the asphalt surface. And I can easily say that in 95 per cent of cases, we did find it at the place of impact. However, there were cases in which it ricocheted depending at which angle it hit the surface and what kind of surface was involved, because mortar shells have enough power that they can simply penetrate the upper layer of the asphalt and become deeply embedded in the asphalt; that is, their tail-fin. So you can always see this trace and it also facilitated our investigation. I say facilitated in terms of determining the type of the shell used in the particular incident.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Prosecutor, can I put some more questions directly to the witness that might facilitate this. Mr. Witness, if you find the tail-fin embedded in the crater, are you then able to determine the angle of descent of the mortar as it hit the ground? Is that a possible indication of the angle of descent. And, secondly, if the tail-fin is not found, then how would you normally determine the kind of mortar that you have -- that have you investigated?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Based on the traces and clues found on the spot, if you find the tail-fin in the centre of the crater, it is possible to determine the descent angle by applying the method that we also used. You take a protractor; and by using geometry, you determine the arms of the angle, and then you calculated the sine and the cosine of the angle and, therefore, you get the angle of the descent. If, however, we did not find the tail-fin at the point of impact, we usually did recover other fragments of disintegrated body of the shell. In that case, a criminal investigation technician retrieves the evidence and proceeds with sending them to the experts from the KDZ; that is, the countersabotage department. Based on that, they reach a unanimous opinion of what type of shell was involved and also based on the size of the damage because an 82-millimetre creates smaller damage than that created by 120-millimetre shell. So based on their findings an opinions and after coordinating and dovetailing them with our opinions, a final report is prepared.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, once you have determined the angle of descent and you know the kind of mortar that you are dealing with, does that enable you to determine the distance from which the mortar was launched? Now, you have the incoming -- the direction of fire, you had the angle of descent, and you have the impacts on the ground. Would that enable you, normally, to determine the distance from which the mortar was fired?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is possible, and that is the domain of the ballistics by using tables relevant for the weapon used and the charge used. However, this was not our job. This was the job of other experts. We only determined the direction and the type of the shell. I was never involved in determining based on the input parameters the origin of fire.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Who would do that in your teams.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Normally, the KDZ had an expert team support by mechanics, professors from the university involved in ballistics and rocket science and things like that, so they helped them in the process.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Were they present at the crime scenes normally, or were they back in their offices?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Usually, the KDZ had their people along with us. However, these expert analysis were conducted in their laboratories.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Prosecutor. Thank you, Mr. Witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Tapuskovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, in order not to go back to this issue, His Honour Judge Harhoff asked another question that witness failed to respond and that deals with the calibre. Your Honour, you asked about the calibre of the shell, didn't you? So I would kindly ask the witness to give his response. What was the calibre of this shell.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: I was going to ask the witness that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: I think he answered. Well, yes, please, put the question to him again. I'm satisfied as to the answer he gave to me. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Witness, what calibre of the shell was this, the incident that we see here.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: It is difficult to say by looking at the photograph, but I remember this particular instance and that was an 82-millimetre shell.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And just in follow-up to His Honour's question regarding the angle of descent. If a tail-fin was not embedded in the asphalt, could an angle of descent nevertheless be determined?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: Yes. I just mentioned that we use the method of an extra stick that was placed in the centre of the crater that had a certain depth, and by that you get one leg of the triangle and then you calculate a cosine of the hypotenuse by using mathematical method.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Can I now ask that we move to photograph -- photograph 5, please. 6, actually. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mr. Sabljica, what do we see here?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: These are mechanical traces on asphalt caused by an impact of a mortar shell. We can see the tail-fin of the shell in the centre of the crater and also you see a metal rod stuck in the crater, and there's a chalk-marked arrow which indicates the direction of fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mr. President, I ask that this photograph be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As P572, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: It's occurring to me, Witness, that this might be a good example and an opportunity for you to explain the science behind this. How were you able to determine the direction of fire as represented by this arrow?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If you allow me, I would respectfully correct you. I think it would be better if I explained to you how a descent angle is measured, because this is a close-up photograph of the centre of the crater. Therefore, these fragmentation traces in the shape of a fan cannot be quite clearly seen here. If you wish, I can explain to you how a descent angle is calculated because that was precisely the purpose of this photograph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Sachdeva.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mr. President, I'm happy for the witness to explain how to establish the angle of descent. I was going to show the witness another photograph and again for him to comment on establishing the direction of fire.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, okay. Let him explain then the descent angle.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Witness, from this photograph, as you were saying, please explain how would you come to the angle of descent?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: May I use this pen?

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: Given that this is the centre of the crater created by a mortar shell, we use a metal rod which shows the hypotenuse of the triangle that it forms, the distance between the impact and the centre of the crater you measure by using a triangle or any other measures device, and therefore you get one element, X. If you know what kind of projectile is involved, and I cannot say precisely judging by this photograph whether there was a 82 or 120-millimetre shell because it's too close for me to determine that. We use the tables used by the JNA, and we knew the size and the dimension of the projectile. We use a dimension from the top of the fuse to the middle of the shell which is stated in the table and we get the height H, and we get the standard formula cosine of Alpha equals H over X. And with the help of this rod, we can determine the descent angle with the accuracy and margin of error of plus/minus two per cent.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mr. President, this explanation is contained in a diagram that has been tendered through a previous witness. Because it involves going from one exhibit to another exhibit, I can show the witness currently this diagram and ask him to confirm if that is the mathematical equations that he is talking about, if that would help.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Firstly, I would like to have this photograph admitted into evidence, Mr. President, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: It's admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As P573, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And if I could ask for 65 ter 84 to be brought up, and I would ask for page -- it's either 12 or 13 of that exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Witness, do you see that diagram on the screen?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And was that the equation you were speaking about beforehand?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: Yes. That is what I explained a while ago. This was normally done by our colleagues from the KDZ as part of a composite report. They prepared this kind of charts and additional drawings because in some cases, when a tail-fin couldn't be found, they provided this calculation of the angle of descent.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Would you be able to explain that diagram?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: Certainly. As I explained previously on the photograph, you see on this chart. The centre of the impact is the tip of the shell. One dimension down there is X. That's from the centre of impact to --

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Once second, Mr. Sabljica. I'm going to ask you to mark -- as you speak, I'll ask you to mark that. First, mark the centre of impact of the shell.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: There it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Maybe we should scroll the picture up a bit --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: -- so we can see the X.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: If that could be done, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Little bit more. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: That will be it, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And where is the centre of the projectile, centre of the shell?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: The centre of the projectile is here. That created a central crater that has certain dimensions, if you look at the cross-section.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Sorry. Did you mark the centre of the projectile?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Or is that the centre of the impact?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: Centre of the explosion, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: What's the circle? You see the circle in the projectile where these dotted lines stem from? What is that circle?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: That little circle is the crossing point of those lines that are created by other traces evolving from the central crater which itself was developed by the impact of the shell. And they provide us with the dimension of the hypotenuse necessary to calculate according to this formula.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: You say, "the other traces evolving from the central crater." Can you mark on the diagram where those other traces are or where those traces are depicted, please.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: It's here. That's their depth in the asphalt of the central crater.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And from -- from the other traces that you just marked, as opposed to the central crater, you'll see two dotted lines that are -- that go back into the projectile. You see a small circle in the middle of the projectile itself.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: You mean this one here?

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: In the projectile, yes. What is that?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: It's the denomination of the crossing point where these transverse lines meet in one point. Probably the colleague who did this sketch marked the point where these lines meet, and that will be the beginning of the distance from the tip of the projectile from the centre of the shell that is necessary for this equation. Since he knew which type of projectile was involved, he could calculate this dimension and place it in the formula, in the equation, H1.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: So the small circle is the centre of the shell? That's what I wanted to ask.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: Approximately. That's the focal point.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Unless there are any further questions from the Bench, Mr. President, Your Honours, I will tender this diagram into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We admit it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As P574, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, please, if the stabilising fin is not found, in the case where it is not found, isn't it difficult to find the centre of the shell, and thus to calculate figure H as well as to find out the X. What do you think of it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] X is easily calculated on the spot. You can calculate -- you can measure the dimensions of the crater to get it. But if you don't find the tail-fin, then based on other evidence, other traces, fragments, parts of the fuse that are often found on the place of impact, other shrapnel, experts of countersabotage protection determine the type of the projectile in their laboratory; and then using their tables that were taken over from the JNA, tables of mines and shells used in mortars, it is very easy to calculate these dimensions because they are given in tables; H, for instance, or a distance from the centre of gravity to the tip of the shell. This particular chart was not done on the spot. It was done in the laboratory using the tables, knowing the type of the projectile.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: May I ask the registrar to bring up again 65 ter 2112, and I'd like to move to photograph 8, please. And can it be moved -- can it be scrolled a little bit to the right, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Okay. Witness, you see a photograph on the screen?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And -- well, just explain what you see here.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: We see the mechanical traces created by the impact of a mortar projectile on an asphalt surface that has spread in the form of an irregular ellipsis. We see the fragments, the tail-fin, and I see a pair of shoes worn by a person standing there.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And do you see -- there appears to be chalk around some of the traces; do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: Yes. This is an initial stage of the on-site investigation. Traces are first marked on the asphalt surface by chalk so that those transverse lines can be drawn to the -- to the centre.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And from this photograph, one can see that the preponderance or the majority of the traces are on the side closest -- on the side towards the right on the photograph. What would that tell you about the direction of fire?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: This photograph is not really perfect for determining the exact direction, but the traces on that side where they are spread more extensively show where the shell came from. From the other angle where the person is standing, it would have been impossible to determine with the methods that we used.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Can you just take a pen and draw roughly the direction of fire?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: With the proviso, as I say again, this photograph is not perfect. There are probably other traces on this side so it would be easier if it wasn't so close up, but the traces that are spread in this way make it possible to draw it this way. I'm ruling out the other side, of course. I'm not talking that into account.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: That is what I essentially want to the achieve. The other side is ruled out; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: Yes, precisely. Because the impact of the explosion was upward.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mr. President, I tender this photograph into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: It's admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As P575, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Can I ask now that Prosecution Exhibit 378, under seal, be brought up.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mr. Sabljica, I'm just going to show you a document in a moment, and I will ask you a few questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: It's not being broadcast, is it?

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Do you see a document there on the screen, Witness?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: Yes, I can see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And what is this document?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: It's an official report of the crime investigations inspector who was on the spot performing a on-site investigation together with a mixed team of employ employees of the Security Services Centre.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Do you see your name there in the middle?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: Yes, of course, under number 3.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: May I just inquire, is there an English translation? If we could go to the next page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Witness, at the end of the, I guess, the first paragraph, you'll see the words -- it talks about the angle of descent, and it says that the shell arrived from north, five degrees west. Do you see that there?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: Yes, I've read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: What does that mean, "north, five degrees west"?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: After completing the determining of the direction, as I explained before, in the kit used by ballistic experts and the scene-of-crime officers, there is a map of the city, a street finder, and a compass. On the street finder, you locate the exact spot as far as the scale enables us, the exact spot where the shell hit, then the north is found on the map using the compass; and then by drawing a line on the ground, you make it coincide with the direction of north. In this case, the angle was five degrees to the north in relation to west. That's very simple.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Sorry. I heard on the translation that it said it was five degrees to the north in relation to the -- in relation to the west. Do you mean five degrees to the north in relation to west, or do you mean five degrees to the west in relation to north?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: From north to west, that's the direction of north-west. It's five degrees from north. We always measured from north, to calculate the degree shown on the compass.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Thank you for that clarification. And this report pertains the Livanjska Street incident at number 26, doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: If I were to show you a map, would you be able to mark, firstly, the rough location of Livanjska Street, and then would you be able to draw a line in the direction of five degrees from north to the west?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: I'll try. I think I could.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Could I ask that the street map 2872 be shown on the screen, please. Can the top right-hand side be enlarged, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Okay. Mr. Sabljica, do you see where Kosevsko Brdo or Livanjska Street is?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: This is Kosevsko.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And, if you can, mark where Livanjska Street is.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: Is it possible to enlarge this section a little more, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Can the map be enlarged a bit more, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: To the right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Can we move it to the right, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Is that clearer?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: Yes, yes. [In English] This is Livanjska Street.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Can you just mark -- can you mark that with an L.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This red line I drew, that's Livanjska Street.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And with a dotted line, can you mark the direction from which the projectile came; and that is, five degrees west of north?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: First, I shall mark the direction of north, and the football stadium is of assistance. The direction of north is this, and this would be a five-degree angle in relation to north. That's the direction from which the shell came.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mr. President, I tender this still into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We admit it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As P576, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: May I now ask for 65 ter 00084 to be brought up, and pages 8 and 9.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mr. Sabljica, do you see a document on the screen?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: I see one half of it because the other half is covered by the map.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And what is this document, please?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: I see the document now. It's a report of the scene-of-crime officer, and that's an integral part of the documentation that he is required to write up after performing an on-site investigation.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Does it pertain to the Livanjska Street incident at number 26?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: Yes, that is clearly indicated. The site of perpetration is Livanjska Street.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mr. President, I tender this document; that is, pages 8 and 9 of 65 ter 00084, into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor, do we have the same document on each side of the monitors?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, it's not the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: The translation is the wrong one.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: The translation is page 6.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think the translation is there now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: If that is fine, then I tender pages 8 and 9 of 65 ter 84 into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We admit it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As P577, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, this incident at 1525, at Livanjska Street 26, do you recall if UNPROFOR also conducted an investigation?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: The UNPROFOR expert teams were usually present on such sites, and I believe they were there as well, if I remember well. But they do their own independent investigation and then at the end they discuss their findings with us, but that depends on the disposition of their commanders.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And with respect to -- to this shelling, the first shell at 1525, do you remember whether UNPROFOR came to a conclusion as to the direction of fire; and if they did come to a conclusion, did it correspond to your conclusion of direction of fire?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: I know that we worked at Livanjska Street doing one of the on-site investigations and that an UNPROFOR team was present, but I'm not sure whether this was the one. But I think on Livanjska Street we agreed as far as the direction of fire was concerned, because our debate ceased there concerning the origin of fire. We did not get involved in that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Can I ask that 65 ter 2113 be shown on the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mr. Sabljica, I'm just waiting for the translation in your language to come up. Do you see -- firstly, do you see this is a report from the United Nations Protection Force?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And do you see where it says, "mjesto," which is location. What does it say there?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: "Location, Livanjska Street, BP 915-607."

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And just above that, it talks about the date and time of shelling. Can you read that there?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: Yes. "8th November 1994 at 1523."

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Does this appear to you to refer to the same incident that we've just spoken about that you conducted the direction of fire investigation?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And if we could go to the last page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mr. Sabljica, you see where it says "conclusion."

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And what does it say?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: "Conclusion: It may be concluded that undoubtedly the area is on the Serbian side between Brijeg and Izlaze."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We are at the time for the break, so we will adjourn for half an hour. According to the time allocated, you would have half an hour more.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mr. President, I know I made promises before, but I will finish within the half an hour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I should say in the absence of Judge Mindua, Judge Harhoff and I sit pursuant to the provision the of Rule 15 busy. Mr. Sachdeva.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mr. Sabljica I, have half an hour left so let's try and move as quickly as possible. Before we broke, we were looking at an UN document where it said that the conclusion was that the most suspected area is on the Serbian side between Brijeg and Izlaze, and what I want to ask you is: Well,, firstly, do you know roughly where Brijeg and Izlaze is.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: I know about Orahov Brijeg, probably that is what they were referring to. And Izlaze approximately on that axis and direction that we established. It's the location in the area and I know this suburb. It's a closer to Vogosca municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: I think you have answered the question but just to confirm. The area of Oraho Brijeg and Izlaze, the direction from Livanjska Street to those locations, does that correspond to the direction that you drew on the map a moment ago with respect to the first shell at 26 Livanjska Street?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mr. President, I tender this UN report into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: It's admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As P578, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Could I now ask for 65 ter 63 to be brought up, pages 5 and 6; again, not to the broadcast.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mr. Sabljica, while that is coming up, you told the Court earlier that after the shell that landed at 1525 or so on the 8th of November, there was another shell that landed on Livanjska Street. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: I think there were two more shells. One of them fell onto the asphalt surface, and the other one I think in a garden in front of a house; that is to say, on the soil.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Do you see on the right-hand side of the screen, you see a document in B/C/S. And I want you to just tell the Court had a does that document relate to?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: It's an official report compiled by a criminal investigation inspector with relation to an on-site investigation. It describes the event, the on-site investigation of the -- carried out on the 9th of November, 1994; and as I can see from the document, the shell fell on the 8th of November.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Just for the benefit of the Bench, the English translation is page 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: While that is being brought up, do you see in that document, Mr. Sabljica, your name there?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: Yes. The last-but-one name is "Mirza Sabljica, criminal investigation technician and ballistic expert from the Sarajevo CSB."

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And if we could go to the next page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mr. Sabljica, in the third paragraph from the top on that page, do you see -- do you see where it describes the direction of fire for this incident?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: Yes. It shows that the shell was fired at 20 degrees from north to east.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: What does it exactly say in the report, if you could just read it out, please: "20 degrees ..."

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: "From the east." "Fired from a direction 20 degrees from the east," probably from the general area of Spicasta Stijena, and this is a report compiled by Dragan Miokovic, a homicide inspector who usually acted as a member of our team. So these are his personal suppositions. This -- what it says from the wider area of Spicasta Stijena, I suppose is his presumption.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And when it says "20 degrees from the east," as you told the Court beforehand, when you calculated the direction of fire, you would first indicate where north is and then you would calculate the degrees from the north. Do I take it, then, that the 20 degrees from the east --

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: From the north to the east. I think that Dragan here made a mistake. This is what it should have read. And if you have a ballistic report, I'm sure that it is noted there in a proper and correct way. Because I repeat right, we always took the north as a benchmark and then calculated the rest with respect to the north.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mr. President, I tender this document into evidence, under seal. This is pages 5 and 6 of 65 ter 63.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We admit it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this entire document of 65 ter 00063 is already in evidence as Exhibit D85.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: I'm grateful to the registrar for that. That will save a lot of time. If I can now ask for 65 ter 03041 to be brought up. These are photographs, and if we could go to photograph number 10, please -- well, page 10. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mr. Sabljica, we now see something similar to what we saw before. Can you just for the sake of clarity, can you indicate with a pen - I ask the assistance of the usher - indicate where the preponderance of the mechanical traces can be found.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: They are marked with chalk on the asphalt, and I'm also going to mark them with the pen. This is the damage caused by the impact.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And the vertical stick stemming from the centre of the impact point, does that indicate the direction of fire?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: Yes. That's the direction of fire, after we applied the method that I explained earlier.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mr. President, I tender this photograph into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: It's admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As P579, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: If we can now move to photograph number 15, page 15, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mr. Sabljica, while we're getting to that photograph, do you generally recognise these photographs to be from the second shell that landed on Livanjska Street?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Actually, it's my mistake. Can we just go to the last photograph, 7405.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mr. Sabljica, I know that it -- it's not the clearest of pictures, but are you able to on this photograph indicate with an arrow the direction of fire?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: Yes, I can. This is the very beginning of the on-site investigation. We didn't touch anything pending the arrival of UNPROFOR team that can you see in the picture. Now I'm going to mark the direction; approximately here, where this gentleman is standing.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And can you just place the letter C above the crater that we see there.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: I tender this photograph into evidence, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We admit it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As P580, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mr. President, in the interest of time, I would like to tender the set of photographs for this incident, an incident which the witness has testified to having been involved in the investigation, and that would be the full 65 ter exhibit 03041.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Tapuskovic, any objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the Defence has no objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We admit them.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As P581, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Sabljica, you earlier testified that UNPROFOR was also present in these investigations, and I'm -- I want to ask you with respect to this shell at 1725 hours, did you and the Bosnian police have a discussion with UNPROFOR about the tables that were used for calculations?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: Yes, we did, of course. As you can see, UNPROFOR prepared a comprehensive report. They even tried to identify the zones of the origin of fire. So together we established it was a 82-millimetre mortar shell, and I think that we also agreed on the direction from which the mortar shell came. However, we noticed that the gentleman from UNPROFOR didn't use mortar tables used for mortars produced by the JNA. Instead, they used, I think, some Finnish tables that envisaged different charges and different ranges as opposed the one that was used by the JNA.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Is it possible then to establish an accurate range or to establish the appropriate charge that was used for projectiles that were produced by the JNA with Finnish firing tables?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: I wasn't involved in that. It is possible, though. What we noticed was that maximum charge zero plus six in the Finnish tables has the range twice -- twice the shorter one than those applicable to the mortars produced in -- in the former Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, I'm going to move on to sniping. You testified earlier that you investigated 60 sniping incidents. And I want to ask you about an incident that took place on the 8th of November 1994, involving -- well, firstly, let me ask you: Did you investigate a sniping incident in -- in the general area of Grbavica that took place on the 8th of November, 1994.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: There were several sniping incidents involving Grbavica. I don't know which particular one you had in mind.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Perhaps I'll bring up a report.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: If I could ask for 65 ter 00062 to be brought up on the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Do you see that document there on the right-hand side?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And what does the document relate to?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: It's an official report compiled by a criminal investigation inspector regarding a sniping incident of November the 8th, 1994 in which Nermina Omerovic was wounded. The incident happened on Djure Danicica Street, 9/5, where she was -- where the lady in question was wounded to the head.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Can I just confirm that this is not being broadcast.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And, Mr. Sabljica, at the middle of the page, do you see your name there?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: Yes, under number 6. I was a member of the team. The late Stankov, who used to my mentor, and I were a member of the ballistic part of the team.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Did you then conduct an investigation into this incident. Do you remember conducting an investigation into this incident?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: Based on this report, my memory is refreshed now.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And when you went to the scene, what did you find and what did you do? Very briefly, please.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: We were mostly focussed on the clues and physical evidence that we recovered. I know that there was no -- the windows were not glazed; instead, they were covered with thin wooden panels. We found traces on these panels. They were about 12 millimetres apart, and they were put there instead of glass. The bullet penetrated these panels, hit the woman in the head, and we found it on the carpet in the room. I think it was a tracer bullet because the carpet was burned. We also found a lead charge of the bullet and the casing. We applied a method often used by ballistics in order to determine the direction of sniper fire or fire from infantry weapon by using a piece of string and a metal tube 8 millimetres in diameter. You connect the points of penetration of the bullet, and you can visualize the place from which the bullet was allegedly or probably fired with a margin of error plus/minus ten per cent.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: The pieces of string, which points in particular did you connect?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: We connected the damage on the wooden panels, which was in the shape of an irregular ellipsis, and the trace on the carpet where we found the slug. And we drew the line between these two points, and we inserted this metal tube into the hole into the obstacle. In this case, it was the window covered by wooden panels, and you can you can establish by visioning the direction of the bullet.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And you said that the bullet went through these wooden panels through the lady's head and left a hole on the carpet. Does the fact that the bullet went through the lady's head, would that affect the trajectory of the bullet, in your opinion?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: Not in this case, because the distance was rather short between the place of accident to the next building from which the sniper fired. It's a distance of between 450 to 500 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Which building? You said, "the next building from which the sniper fired." Which building was that?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: The well-known building in Sarajevo known as Metalka.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Why do you say "well-known"?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: There are three buildings that were built at the same time before the war. They have the same structure and the shape; and on the ground floor of that particular building, there used to be company premises of Metalka. That is how it got its name.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Do you know what that building was used for during the war?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: A sniper was usually firing from this building, across the river, targeting the civilians who were under the -- the territory under the control of the Bosnian army.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And the Metalka building under -- which party to the conflict controlled the area where the Metalka building was?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: It's the area of Grbavica controlled by the VRS.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: I'm going to show you a photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: If I could have 65 ter 2 -- firstly, Mr. President, I would like to tender this document into evidence, under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We admit it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As P582, under seal, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And if I could have photograph 2825 shown on the screen. Yes. If we could leave it like that, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mr. Sabljica, do you recognise that photograph, or what's in that photograph?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: Yes, I can. You can see part of Grbavica and Marindvor and the museum on the other side, and the building on Djure Danicica Street and Franje Rackog.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Now, the place that you went to investigate the sniping incident on Djure Danicica Street, can you see the building or the house on that photograph; and if you can, can you please mark it?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: I'm not quite sure whether this number was in this building here or the other building. Anyway, they are all on Djure Danicica Street, and they are close to the river. I'm not sure whether it's the first building or the one next to it. I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Can you just place two letters DD for Djure Danicica in between those two buildings, if you can, please.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Thank you. And can you see where the Metalka building it; and if you can, can you just put a M on it?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: This is the one in the middle.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Now, you said that you conducted up to 60 sniping incidents -- investigations into sniping incidents. Did you ever conduct investigations where -- involving trams.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: Yes, I did, at least a dozen times.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And did you conduct investigations involving trams in locations that can be seen in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: Yes. The trams were the most frequent target in this area. Because there's a curve there, it has to slow down in order to proceed on the other side of the street.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Just indicate where that curve is and where the trams had to slow down.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: I'll put a circle here because this is where the tram tracks make a curve and cross over to the other side of the street, and usually this is where trams were most frequently targeted.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Where would the fire come from?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: The investigation usually established that shots came from the area where the Metalka building is.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And do you remember -- I just want to going to the incident on the 8th of November, 1994. You said a lady was wounded. Do you remember how old this person was?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: I am sorry, but this victim was a girl who was shot in the head and died. She wasn't wounded.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: In the area where she lived where you have marked DD, who lived in those buildings? Were there civilians or were there military people there?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: Civilians, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: When you went to the building to conduct your investigation, did you see any evidence of military personnel or military facilities there?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: Not that I have seen.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mr. President, I tender this photograph into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We admit it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As P583, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And Mr. President, might I just inquire how much time I have left?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: You have actually exhausted the half an hour.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Very well. That is the end of my examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Tapuskovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Sabljica, I appear here for Dragomir Milosevic as Defence counsel, and I would like to question you on certain matters that have been discussed before between you and the Prosecutor. And in the interests of efficiency, I will try to phrase my questions as clearly as possible, and you try to answer as briefly as possible. First of all, I would like to ask you about all these matters that you have discussed with the Prosecutor. You have told us already that you have done a lot of work on shedding light on problems related to shelling. You said that in 90 per cent of your cases you dealt with shells?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: Mortar shells.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: And that you had about 50 cases?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: At least 50 cases.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Since you started working on such cases, as I see from your statement and your prior testimony on the 15th of July, 1993, I would like to know, in fact, could you explain to the Trial Chamber in how many cases you dealt with the problems that you have spoken about from August 1994 to end November 1995?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: It's a very specific question. All right. In that period, there were perhaps around 40 on-site investigations involving civilian deaths that I took part in as a member of the team or as an assistant.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell me with regard to that period, to that time, how many of your cases fell within the period between mid-June and November, or rather, between mid-June until end August 1995? In that period, were there -- was there a preponderance of such incidents?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: Compared to which other period? Compared to the beginning of the war, the middle of the war?

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: If we compare it to the period between beginning of August 1994 until beginning of June?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: Shelling was very frequent in the summer of 1994 until the end of that period you mentioned; maybe 60 per cent of on-site investigations out of the total that I mentioned as the number of cases I participated in.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: And if we talk about your sniping incidents, did you have a single one that you personally helped investigate between May and November 1995?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: I really can't tell you. I don't know, honestly.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: You mean you can't remember?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: I cannot remember a particular incident that stuck in my mind.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell me about this certificate you were issued confirming your qualifications from the job? Who had to authorise it to confirm your qualification?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: I was issued with that certificate from the republic MUP of Bosnia-Herzegovina, the Ministry of the Interior; whereas, in former Yugoslavia, you had to pass the so-called state exam to get that certificate. However, in the conditions of war, the republic Ministry of the Interior of Bosnia and Herzegovina was the establishment that took over the authority to issue the certificate to me, because I was a policeman. I was not a reserve soldier.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: In order to avoid going back to this, could you clarify now: In that case where you worked on a shelling incident, or incidents, the distance to the origin of fire, could it be determined if you didn't know the exact charge the shell had to have in order to have range, the necessary range?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: It's an appropriate question, but I have to tell that you we did not determine in our work the origin of fire. We only determined the direction of fire. Although, I always asked myself that question, the person who fired knows which charge they used. UNPROFOR teams and some other experts have demonstrated that it is possible [Realtime transcript read in error "impossible"] to determine even that, but I myself did not determine such things. I only determined the direction of fire, not the origin of fire.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Sachdeva.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
