utterances.text: I'm sorry, Mr. President. I heard in the translation that the witness said that UNPROFOR teams and some other expert have demonstrated that it is "possible" to determine even that and it's written "impossible." I'm wondering if the witness could clarify.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Did you hear that, Witness?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I understood. I have to go back a few years to the case of Professor Dzalic, a professor of the mechanical engineering faculty of the University of Sarajevo. He was an assistant lecturer. He made a very comprehensive analysis using a lot of evidence, demonstrating that it was possible, and he did it, to determine the origin of fire. I didn't go into that analysis and the resulting debate, so I couldn't tell you how and why.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Sabljica, I didn't even ask you about the theory. The expert who will come to testify soon will do that. I asked you about your practical work. You, who were on the ground, who dealt with such cases daily, you did not determine such things based on the charge of shells. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: No. No. We couldn't do that, because we couldn't determine what the charge was, based on the elements that we examined.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Let me put it this way: In this configuration of the area, you know very well how Sarajevo is situated in that depression surrounded by hills and the deployment of forces on both sides. Let me go back to one question, in fact: Who was on the hills around Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: The army of Republika Srpska, or whichever way you like to call it. There is only one hill that was held by the Bosnian army: Hum and Zuc.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: And who held Stupsko hill?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: It's not in fact a hill, although the word "hill" features in the name, Stupsko Brdo, but it's an elevation of no more than 20 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: On the southern side, who held Mojmilo?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: I am sorry. I forgot about Mojmilo. Mojmilo was held by the Bosnian army. So in the north, they held Hum and Zuc; and in the south they held Mojmilo. That was within the circle, and outside the circle there were other front lines that I did not visit. There was Igman.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Could we say that the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina also held Debelo Brdo?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: You mean the one above Grbavica? Apart of it, yes, but not the higher part. That was under the control of the VRS.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: What about Colina Kapa?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: They had lost that very early on. It was held by the VRS; the small one, in fact. The big part was no man's land for a long time before it was taken by the VRS.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Let me ask you about Grdonj.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: That's where the repeater was, and Bosnian forces were there. Sedrenik was held by the VRS. That was common knowledge.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: I happen to know Sarajevo, and I know certain geographic reference points. Stupsko Brdo and Grdonj, who had the geographic advantage?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: Could the witness repeat the answer?

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: With such configuration of the terrain, and with you determining only the direction -- I'm sorry. The interpreters asked to you repeat your answer to the previous question.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: Grdonj is higher than Stupsko Brdo. It's at a higher altitude.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you for this. Now, with this configuration, with this lay of the land, and with you determining only the direction of fire, wasn't it important and wasn't it necessary to at least try to determine the origin of fire?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: I agree with you that it was important, but the fact remains we didn't do it at the time nor had we orders to do so. At least our team of experts did not deal with determining the origin of fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: You mean to say that even when the forces of the VRS were behind a hill and the hill was held by the Bosnian army, you always assumed that something was fired by the Serbian side?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: I never assumed that, and none of our reports say definitively who fired.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: But it is frequently written, "fired by the aggressor."

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: In reports by other employees of the police, you can see two reports signed by Dragan Miokovic. Unfortunately, I don't have any of my reports. We never assumed anything or jumped to conclusions about who fired which side. We usually gave an indication of an area; for instance, on that side, in that direction, there is a field; in that direction, there is a hill. And if anyone wanted to go further than that, there were other experts, other teams who could do a more detailed analysis.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: We'll go back to a related document, but let me first ask you something else. I want to go as quickly as possible. I want to go through your statement you gave on the of November, 1995, DD00-1950. Can you confirm it's your statement, looking at the cover page?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: Yes, this is my signature. I see the English translation. On the Bosnian version there is no signature, but that is my statement. That's the statement I gave on the 19th of November, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: I have some questions concerning that statement, and that's why I would like the following page shown to you, page 2. If you look at that first sentence, you have already told my learned friend from the Prosecution that before the 15th of July, 1993, you worked in the army?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: I was a regular soldier in the BH army.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: You did not use your professional skills in any way. You were simply a regular soldier?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: You have to take my word for it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: And what positions did you hold?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: I exited the former JNA as a lance corporal. In the BH army, I was -- you mean on what lines I was deployed? Our unit held the line between the Elektroprivreda building to the school of economics from May 1992 -- until May 1992 and then we were moved to Hrasno Brdo, where we stayed until mid-October 1992 until, following which we were on Stup. We worked in stints; seven days on the line and seven days at home, until I transferred to the police force.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Sabljica, could we then say that Hrasno Brdo was also under the control of the BH army?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: Well, the neighbourhoods around Hrasno Brdo, but the -- the thoroughfare was under the control of the VRS. I mean Vojvadanska Street. We held only three streets: Zargorska, Milinklatska, and I don't remember the name of the third one. The main part was under the VRS control.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: But since you were there on Hrasno itself, this is where Dobrinja is. Is it close?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: No, it isn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, Grbavica is close.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: Yes. The Zeljeznicar Football Stadium was a no man's land. We can see it at about 150 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: I do apologise. It means that we overlapping and that we will have to slow down?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: Yes, we both are.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me something about the position of Grbavica. Grbavica was down there at the bottom of the town?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: Yes, right next to the river bank of Miljacka. That is the part of the town that is in the plain, on the flat ground of the city.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: From three sides, Grbavica was surrounded by the BH army?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: Yes, by the BH army.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Apart from that, there is Debelo Brdo above it?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: I said part of it was under the control, and from there they could have the few of the beginning of Zagrebacka Street. It was difficult to control the whole of Grbavica from that point, and I'm talking as a layman.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: While you were there and maybe after that, if you know, there were frequent conflicts there and exchange of fire?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: I know there was fierce fighting up there, but my unit was never on that front line. I told you where we were deployed down there between Elektroprivreda, school of economics and the [indiscernible] part of Debelo Brdo; and after that, the whole unit was redeployed to Hrasno.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know where Sanac is?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: If we have the same thing in mind, it is between the Zeljeznicar Stadium and Vraca.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Who held that?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: I think it was the VRS.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Let's go back to Debelo Brdo now. Beneath Debelo Brdo, how far was the Jewish cemetery from it.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: There's the Bosut barracks, and then below the barracks at some 400 or 500 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Who held the Bosut barracks?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: The VRS.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Where was the barracks located?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: It is in the part of Debelo Brdo. It was well fortified. It is the beginning of the Grbavica, and under it is the Jewish cemetery and Kovacici Settlement. These were the forward front lines.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Who had the dominant point on Debelo Brdo. Was it the BH army?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: To tell you the truth, I don't know. I didn't go to this front line, and I think it was held by the VRS.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Jewish cemetery --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: Could the speakers please repeat what they said at the same time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: The interpreter is asking you to repeat. Ask the question and then we'll get the answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: I asked the witness about the Jewish cemetery.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: It was divided. Half was held by the BH army; half was held by the VRS.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Talking about sniping activity, was it possible, in view of what you said, for sniper to shoot from Debelo Brdo as well? Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: Yes. It was possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Was it possible for snipers to shoot from the Jewish cemetery from both sides?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: It was possible, geographically speaking. You could see these streets from up there.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: At any rate, whoever was on Debelo Brdo had control and commandeering view of Jewish cemetery and Grbavica?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: I suppose so. I didn't go up there, but let us suppose that that is the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Since you were a fighter for a time on Hrasno, I suppose that you know the southern part very well.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: You mean the one facing Vraca.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: Well, relatively well, I could say.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: But also facing Dobrinja and Nedzarici.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: I'm not very familiar with this new part of town. It's always been new to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: It's a new part of town, but it stretches also in the valley?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: That's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: And all of that is below Mojmilo?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: You mean Alipasino Polje and these buildings? Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I'm referring both to the Serbian positions and the BH army positions where the separation line ran below Mojmilo through Hrasno, Dobrinja, Nedzarici? Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: I don't know about this other side. I can only talk about Hrasno and Zeljeznicar Stadium; whereas, where the defence line ran of both part parties in the area of Dobrinja, I don't know. I never went there and never worked there.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: In any case, speaking about these positions, in the core of Sarajevo, in the inner-city where separation lines were, is that true, that there were separation lines in the town itself?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: In the town itself, yes, there were separation lines.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: During the time of your military service, there were constant conflicts along the separation lines?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: I can say that I was, to a certain extent, fortunate with my unit that we weren't solved in so many incidents, because this line that runs along the river Miljacka was rather peaceful. However, there were skirmishes an occasional shootings on other lines that were close to our position.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Is it fair to say that neither army practically did not fire at separation line; instead, whenever they operated, they were active in the depth of the territory?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: I cannot confirm that. You'd better ask that of an officer or a general. I don't know anything about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Let us now move to specific issues that my learned colleague Sachdeva asked you about. You were --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Tapuskovic, bear in mind the purpose for which this witness is here. He is here to testify. He is an expert in a particular area.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I believe that this witness is an eye-witness. He is not here in the capacity, as far as I can understand, of an expert. He is giving evidence about the things that he was involved in as someone who was present at the scenes. In addition to that, he was a fighter for a certain period of time, and he can give us some explanations about the issues that I asked him about, which are relevant. He himself said that he was a soldier. I didn't know that. I will move now to specific incidents. I was about to do that, but he is just a witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. He is a witness, but stay close to the incidents in relation to which he can actually testify.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: You said that --

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will try to be as quick as possible, Your Honours. That is why I dwelled on this previous issues, and I'm will certainly not consume all the time that my learned friend the Prosecutor used.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, you spoke about sniping and shelling incidents. Let me start with sniping incidents, first, because you mentioned more about them in your statement. And here, at the beginning of the second paragraph, you say - I presume you still have the statement in front of you - . "I have done a lot of investigations since July 1993. We always worked in a team, and usually there were two ballistics experts."

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: Two ballistics experts were involved in most serious cases. Mr. Stankov and Mr. Medjedovic, as you could have seen earlier, were involved in the Livanjska incident when two shells were fired.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: In order not to go back to this statement again, let me ask you this, and it's mentioned in the second part of your statement. Here you say, in the second part, below this dotted line in the middle of the page, at the very end of the first paragraph: "It was impossible to determine the calibre of the weapon because the bullets fragmented." You mentioned an incident of 9th November, 1994. My question is: As you said, you were involved in ballistic examinations. When a bullet dispersed and becomes fragmented, it is possible at all to establish the calibre?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: No. It was not possible, and that's what we said. I don't remember this particular incident to tell you the truth, but of course it is impossible to determine the calibre, unless you have at least a core the bullet. If you only have the casing and other small pieces, it's impossible.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Least of all the direction?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: Yeah. The direction can be determined on the basis of other elements based on the obstacle was hit, based on the entry holes or the holes op the clothes of the victims and other things. Direction is something completely different. However, for the determining the calibre, you at least have to have the bigger part of the bullet in order to be able to even discuss the calibre.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: I'm asking you about this because what you said in the next paragraph: "It was not possible to establish the precise origin of fire because the car was driving very fast." This is what you said. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. The car was driving fast; and in that case, it would involve a wide range not only plus/minus ten degrees. And one would prejudge any conclusions, and we would be precluded from drafting an accurate report.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, basically speaking, that should have applied to every car and vehicle on the move.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: Well, yes, basically speaking.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I'm going to pose my questions in relation to specific incidents. Let us now move on to the incident of 8th November, 1994. And that's document -- Prosecution document, under seal, 582, 65 ter 0062. You have been shown this document today.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, Your Honours, lest I forget. This statement that I just showed to the witness, can it be admitted into evidence?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As D168, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: This is a Prosecution Exhibit, and this is, as you can see, the official report. This little girl was killed on the 8th of November; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: Yes. We came to the scene the day after.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: This report reads that it was done not on the following day because, as you said, it was impossible to conduct an on-site investigation.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: Because of the firing, the on-site investigation was conducted on the 12th of November, 1994. Yes. This was probably drafted by a homicide inspector. I don't know who signed it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: We could say then it was four days later?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: Well, that's what's written there.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Now, could you please focus on the last paragraph. It says, that what you noted is, last paragraph on the first page.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: I see.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: "On the window of the room, looking in the direction of Grbavica, instead of glass, there was plywood."

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: It was not plywood. It was thin wood. Otherwise, it wouldn't have held, and those were two panels with an open space in between of ten to 12 millimetre; rather thin. The person who report this report - and this is not my report; it is Mr. Stankov's - said that it was a wooden plate. He wrote plywood instead. Plywood is something quite different.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: I have a reason for asking you this.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: We speak the same language, regardless of this term B/C/S and its various variants.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: I agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: But in that language, plywood has a very specific meaning. It's rather thick wood. Would you agree?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: Yes, yes. And it's manufactured using special technology. We could say that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: On the 12th of November, it was noted that the windows were boarded up with plywood, which is thick wood. Could you tell me how could something like that have been written, while you now describe it as thin wood?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: It's not me who wrote that. It's not my report.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Sabljica, you see all the names of people who were involved in this on-site investigation, and it says, under number 6, "Mirza Sabljica."

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: I did attend, but the report was written up by a criminal investigations inspector, and he used his own words to describe what he found on the scene. In my report, I certainly didn't write that it was plywood. It wouldn't have looked the same after the impact of a bullet. It would have been the plate was there was deformed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: You just said -- state a fact. But you also - I mean your team - note here that not only was there plywood, but on the window on the outside there was also a wooden blind. That's another obstacle? Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: But the blind was not pulled down, and that's not written here.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: It's not written here, and it couldn't have been omitted, if what you say is true. So you say it's incorrect?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: There was -- there were shutters. There was a blind, but it doesn't say whether it was opened or closed. And it was open all the time, because at the beginning of the war it had been detached by shelling.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Now, if we read on, it says in your official report: "On the floor, on the carpet below the window, a blood-stain was found."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Sachdeva has a point.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Just a small clarification, Mr. President. It's not his official report, at least the report that is being spoken about right now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Very well, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, Your Honours, up to now, in the course of our work over the past few months, never, ever have we dealt with a report that was signed by all eight members of a team. This report was done by a team consisting of eight persons, including Mirza Sabljica, and it would be illogical now to look in this report for all the eight signatures of all the eight persons involved. Does the Prosecutor perhaps challenge the authenticity of this report; otherwise, what have we been doing all this time? Unless we were dealing with reports made jointly by teams.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Sachdeva.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mr. President, of course, I'm not challenging the authenticity of this report. I'm simply saying, in fact, what the witness said himself that yes. He attended this investigation, but he did not draft there particular report. It doesn't mean to say that it's not authentic. And, of course, the line of questioning is perfectly appropriate. But just to be clear, when you talk about a report and when you say it's his report, technically that is just not right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, the point is taken. Let's move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't want to go deeper into this debate, but I can't believe my ears.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: You are not going to go anymore into it. Let's move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: "On the floor, on the carpet below the window, a blood-stain was found." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: Yes, it's written there. "Of an irregular shape and dimensions were 50 by 60 centimetres."

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: I quote on: "Also on the carpet, next to the table, traces of burning were noted; and from those traces from the carpet, a fragment of a bullet was extracted" Is that written there?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: Yes, that's what is written there.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: It's written there?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: You confirm a moment ago that a bullet was extracted, but here it says "part of a bullet"; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: Yes, part of the core of the bullet, and the casing that burst and fragmented was not found.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: So it's in relation to that part of the bullet that you determined the direction?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: It was one of the reference points.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: And there were other reference points.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: On the wooden plates, we attached this piece of string through a tube, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Was it a piece of string or something made of glass?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: You take this length of string, put it through a tube, you attach it to the points; and then when you look through the tube, you can do the sighting and determine the direction.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: It reads on: "On the floor next to the bookshelf, a part of the copper casing was found."

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: You didn't use it as a reference point for anything?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: No. Those were traces that probably burst in impacting the head of the victim. That's my assumption at least.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Now pay attention to this part, to this sentence: "In the plank in the bookshelf above the TV set, a lead part of the round of the bullet was found embedded."

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: I don't remember that. Possibly.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Wasn't this found embedded -- wasn't that the core of the bullet?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: If that was just the part of the bullet, and in this other spot, we found the lead part of the bullet, at least the part of it, how is it possible that you didn't use it as a reference point for determining the direction of fire?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: I believe the technician, in fact, the inspector, who wrote this report, erroneously indicated the location of various parts of the bullet. The core was found in the carpet and another fragment was probably stuck in the bookshelf.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: So you are now claiming that what was found in the carpet, according to the report, was in fact found in the bookshelf; and vice versa, the fragment found on the bookshelf was in fact the one that was embedded in the carpet?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: So what was used as a reference point? The lead part of the bullet or the other fragment?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: One point was on the carpet; the other point was in the wooden plate. Those were the points linked by the string. We didn't do anything with the bookshelf. It was not an element in our examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Let us clarify this. This lead part was in the carpet.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: Yes. The core of the bullet was in the carpet. If you allow me, usually, these reports are accompanied by the ballistic report that was signed by Mr. Stankov, me, and other experts involved. In the Galic case, these other reports were also attached.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: So, in this most important part of this report, we have a piece of information that is absolutely not consistent with what you found on the scene?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: And if the reference point used was the one on the bookshelf above the TV set, if that had been used, then you would have gotten a horizontal alignment of the direction of the bullet?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: I don't know. I didn't do that. What could have been if it had been? You are jumping at the gun a bit.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: I will put it to you, and that's my right, that you came to the scene where a young girl was tragically killed with the intention to show that the bullet could not have come from any other place than the one you ended up indicating?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: I didn't come to the location with that intent. I came to determine the direction of fire and a possible location from which it could have been fired.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: If the lead part of the bullet was stuck in the bookshelf, then we could in no way claim that it come from Metalka.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: Metalka building is right across that building. It could only have come from a lower floor. However you look at it, whatever the alignment, the bullet had come from that building. It looks directly at the building of the victim. If you used a different reference point, you could have obtained perhaps a lower position of the origin of fire. The trajectory we obtained was downward. If we had used the piece in the bookshelf, you would have gotten maybe a flatter horizontal line, but it would again lead to the Metalka building.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: It's time for the break. We'll adjourn.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Tapuskovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Could we say, Mr. Sabljica, that whatever it was, plywood, blinds, shutters, or a thinner plate of wood, wherever the bullet had come from, from the spot where it was fired, the room cannot be seen on the inside?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: We could say so.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Could we then say that that girl could certainly not have been a target of a direct attack and hit in the way in which she was killed?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: If the shooter couldn't see her, then she couldn't have been a direct target.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: If we could look again at the second page, and I would like to deal with the report for a little longer. It says at the very beginning: "The scene, as well as all the traces found, have been photographed." Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: Yes. The scene-of-crime officer has to do that. That's his job.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Was the spot where the first fragment of the bullet was found photographed?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: I suppose so. If the scene-of-crime officer did his job properly, then that should have been the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Was the spot photographed, the bookshelf above the TV set?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: Probably. I haven't seen those photos.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Is there a photograph of the black hole in the plywood?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: I'm saying again, it should be among the photographs of the scene.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, if it had been indeed plywood, and we know the thickness of plywood, would the bullet have pierced it?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: No. I told you. It couldn't have pierced it and it wasn't plywood.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: And can you tell me, is there a photo documentation of this?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: I don't know. I haven't seen it. This is a 13-year-old case. There must be. There should be. I left the police force in 1996.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: This child that was killed, you photographed her in the mortuary, I mean someone from your team?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: Probably. It's written there. I think the scene-of-crime officer should have done that. That was the usual procedure.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: In principle, throughout your work, from the first case to the last, be it shelling or sniping, did you ever photograph a victim on the scene?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: Yes. There were cases where we found corpses on the scene. We sometimes examined scenes where there was a body.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: What about the cases that you talked about in your evidence, Livanjska Street and the other cases discussed? Were there any corpses on the scene?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: No, not as far as I know. When we did our examinations, the corpses had already been removed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: You must understand that I'm not questioning in any way the tragedy of it, especially in the case of such a small girl. But the place where it happened was practically on the separation line?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: Well, if you look at it, yes. Grbavica begins on one side of the river and the Djure Danicica Street was on the other side of the Miljacka River, but people inhabited these buildings, at least the area controlled by the BH army; of course, at their own risk.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell that due to the proximity of the front line, it was possible, not only in the case of this little girl, that as a result of exchange of fire it could have happened that somebody got killed. Were there such cases?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: Yes, there were.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Can you explain a couple of things to me with regard to the photograph showing the Metalka?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: Be my guest.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Do you see -- do you see the photograph?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: Yes, I do. It's in front of me.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Do you see the letter D, indicating one of the buildings?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: I don't see a single letter on my photograph, if we are looking at the same photograph, that is.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: I can see it on my screen. There's a letter D. Oh, I'm sorry. It's just a red -- red surface. Do you know who was -- is this building behind the Metalka?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: You mean what army --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Sachdeva.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mr. President, before counsel continues, I'm just a little bit concerned that the photograph that the witness marked -- that his markings have not been recorded as was the case yesterday. Can I just confirm with the registrar if that is not the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: His markings were recorded, and they were recorded as Exhibit P583. And if Defence counsel would like the markings to be shown, we can do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: I'm grateful to the registrar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Tapuskovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like my case manager to show me this photograph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Is it you want to have the photograph with the markings?

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I didn't receive the translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Do you wish to have the photograph that you marked? P583.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Sabljica, you marked in the photograph the place from which you assess a gunshot came.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: The Metalka, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: And you marked the location where the window was through which, as you say, this girl was shot.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: Yes. But only I'm not sure, as I said, whether it was the first or -- building or the one next to it. In any case, it is Djure Danicica Street. You see these two red dots.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me behind this building, these rectangle building were belonging to the BH army?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: No. They were all under the control of the VRS, except for the front one that resembles Metalka, and half of the building was practically no man's land. Both parties used to take position there is but those were not permanent positions, as much as I was able to gather with regard to the situation on the front.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Can you mark this building?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: With colour blue.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: [In English] May I? [Interpretation] This is the one, and I will mark it with an arrow. This is the building that was subject to constant incursions by members of both armies.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. That's the building where the point of the arrow is.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: Yes, this whole building. In actual fact, it was never under permanent control by either side, as much as I can remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: And this building located behind it, and there is the one that leans on the Metalka and there's another one behind it, were you aware that BH army had positions there?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: You mean this new red one?

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: I don't think so. All this area was under the control of the VRS, as much as I was able to tell.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. In any case, from this location where, as you say the BH army was occasionally, was this position in the same place as the position viewed from the Metalka with regard -- with respect to the flat where the girl was?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: No. It is more to the left, viewed from that point. So the line of sighting, if you make it, you don't have this building in your field of vision, and therefore we ruled it out immediately. Maybe this photograph doesn't show it precisely. If you had a photograph made from a different angle, it would have given you a better pick of how dominate the Metalka is over the buildings on Djure Danicica Street.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Can we say that you immediately ruled it out, primarily because those were the BH army positions?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: Absolutely not. I repeat, again, at least black expert team never went to carry out an investigation with intention to blame any party. We wanted to do our job professionally, and we wanted the reports to be integral part of the files for some future trials. No one ever assumed that this is how it was going to end.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: And my last question concerning this document. Can you explain at all how these drastic changes occurred in your evidence compared to this report, and I'm talking about the plywood, the shutters, the traces of bullets, et cetera. How is it possible that now you are saying that this is inconsistent with this document?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: First of all, I didn't compile this report, and maybe I can explain to you the procedure. It was only part of the report that was used for the purpose of investigation, conducted and directed by a an investigating judge. An integral part to every report in addition to the criminal inspector's report, who notes down facts in his notebook, he extracts some information from ballistic experts, arrives at his own conclusions, writes the report in his office, and signed it. Based on the accurate methods that we employed, we reached valid conclusions both mechanical and ballistical. And in addition to the criminal investigation technician's report, we submitted all the material. I will go back, again, in time. For fire years, in the Galic case, I solely spoke about my own reports that I signed myself. Therefore, I didn't change what I said before, but, rather, these are the facts that were written down by my colleague, based on his own conclusions.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Can we then conclude that everything that is written here does not reflect the actual state of affairs?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: I wouldn't agree with that completely. There are some accurate things; but as for traces produced by fire-arms, I wouldn't agree on that section. I would have preferred to have a report written by my deceased colleague, which is also an integral part of this case file, so that we can make a comparison.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: From this report, as we can see, there are Borislav Stankov and Mirza Sabljica, who are ballistic experts, and these two involved in the investigation and their names are listed as members of the team that stands behind this report?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: But they didn't sign the report.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I think this is enough on this subject. Since we don't have much time left, if we can clarify these matters relating to the Livanjska Street that we devoted most attention to, or rather, the Prosecution devote the most attention to.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If we look at this document, DD00-85, page -- Please, can we receive this photograph with the markings as a Defence exhibit. The photograph is still on our screens.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. We will admit it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As D169, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness please take a look at the document D85. It's already been shown today by the Prosecutor. Let us go to page 5; English page 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: This is about an official report dated 9th of November, and it relates to Livanjska Street, number 36.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: According to this report, this event took place at around 1730 hours, and you visited the scene at 9.00 on the 9th of November, 1994.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: Yes, that is what is written here.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: And we can see you acted as an expert in ballistics?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: If we look at page 2, and in order to save time, it says that the official report was compiled by Dragan Miokovic?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, you also didn't sign this report. It was signed by Dragan Miokovic. But as a member of this team, do you stand behind the report.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: I would have to first read it in its entirety. And I'm telling you, again, a ballistics report was an integral part, as a rule, of every; report, and if that was the case, I could stand behind what Dragan Miokovic said?

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: In other words, it is possible that you may contend something from this report, and therefore you would disagree?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: It depends on your questions. If there is some disputable issue that I can remember, then that will be acceptable. But if I cannot remember something, then I wouldn't contend it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we look now at page 2 to see if there are any issues in dispute. There it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: If you look at paragraph 3 in B/C/S version, it says: "The MUP RBH and the OSB Sarajevo learned that the shell was fired from a direction 20 degrees from the east, probably from the wider area of Spicasta Stijena occupied by the aggressor."

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: I immediately noticed a mistake. It says "20 degrees from the east," and I think I replied and discussed this with the Prosecutor. It should read, "20 degrees from the north to the east," because I said we always decided the angle with reference to the north. And, probably, the second part that mentioned Spicasta Stijena was probably personal assessment of Mr. Miokovic. We just noted that this or that area was there. So the only mistake here is that it should read "20 degrees from the north to the east."

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Can we say then that this is not true --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: What do you mean from the north to the east? Is that the same thing as north-east?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, precisely so. We always marked north in the map of the city; and then with regard to the north, we decided the direction of fire. So that would be approximately north, north-easterly direction, if you take into consideration this is 20 degrees.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, I understand now. 20 degrees from the north to the east.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Can you then explain why the report simply says 20 degrees from the east? You say it's a mistake.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that this is a mistake, an unintentional one, of course. An unintentional mistake on the part of Mr. Miokovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: It's a very bad mistake.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Because if you go into ballistic reports, nothing was ever determined using east as a reference point. It's always the north and this --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: This 20 degrees from the east could also take you in the direction of the south, conceivably.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Correct. Perfectly right.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I continue?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Can we then say it's an error?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: If I understood correctly what you said, even the reference to Spicasta Stijena is a mistake?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: It's a free assessment of the inspector who authored this. He's prejudging the conclusions as to the possible origin of fire without having been able to determine anything precisely, and he didn't possess the methods. It is in the broader area. He could have phrased it differently.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: But you disagree even with that.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: I agree that it's in that area, the area of Spicasta Stijena, But from which position it was fired is another matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, that's what I'm trying to say. You disagree with his assessment?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: I don't agree with his assessment, phrased this way, at least.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Towards the end of this official report, it says: "The head of the UNPROFOR investigation team was Colonel Renuits [phoen]?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: I don't remember his name. All I know was he was a Frenchman. He frequently led those teams. I think it was a ballistic expert himself specialising in artillery, I believe.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: And again, towards the end. It says, that by comparing the findings of the MUP team on the one hand and the UNPROFOR team on the other hand, it was determined that the direction of fire of shells including those that fell next to 36 were identical as determined by both teams?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: Yes. We completely agreed on the fact that it was 20 degrees north to east, and we didn't discuss the origin of fire at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: And that relates to the event that happened at 1730?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: Yes, the one that happened outside number 36. Is that it?

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, could the witness be shown photograph P575.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Can I ask the witness something. Suppose you're able to identify that the missile or shots came from 160 degrees south, would you still describe it as 160 degrees from the north to the south? It would be very near to the south, to 180 degrees, just 20 degrees from the south, you know. So because you're telling us that you always start from the north, you would --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I don't understand that. Because if it's 160 degrees, only 20 degrees from the south, why would you say 160 degrees from the north to the south when it is so near to the south?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We've always used the same terminology so that findings be compatible, because the map would be always oriented to the north, using compass. And even if it's a bit closer to the south, we don't say it's 20 degrees from south. We say 160 from north.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Am I right, Mr. Prosecutor and Mr. Tapuskovic, isn't this the first time that we're being told that this is how maps are read -- were read by the authorities in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mr. President, all I can say is that whether it is -- in my submission, it's a question of terminology. And whether it's 160 degrees from the north or south from the north or -- sorry, 20 degrees from the south or 160 degrees, the direction of the angle is still going to remain the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Can we just find the statement which the witness corrected, which said 20 degrees east. Can you put that on the screen, because what I'm trying to see is in the absence of that explanation, how would we have interpreted that? In the absence of his explanation that it is in fact 20 degrees from the north to the east, how would we have read the simple phrase 20 degrees east?

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mr. President, that's, indeed, why the explanation was sought from the witness, and I would also add that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: But doesn't it have an implication for what we have been doing?

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: What I would say is that when you have, at least in this incident and also in the Markale incident, for example, you have very clear craters that have been formed on the asphalt, and the Prosecution's submission is that there is within the range of five to ten degrees -- there is only one possible direction of fire that can be ascertained. And the witness, Richard Higgs, who is coming on Monday will explain all of this. And whether it's a question of terminology, where you say 20 degrees west of north or 170 degrees, it doesn't change the calculations -- the scientific calculations that are made when you see a crater on the ground. And so the expert will hopefully make this clearer to you, Mr. President and Your Honour, Judge Harhoff.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: But could I perhaps just ask the witness why -- why is it that you did not use the ordinary measurement by the compass; this is to say, to use the 360 degree all around. And so if a shot came from almost the south, you would say that simply it came from the direction of 160 degrees, or as we had an example just a while ago, that you had an indication of something being shot from a position five degrees to the west. That, in my view, would perhaps more clearly be referred to as a direction of 355 degrees. So why is it that you did not use the ordinary compass indication? Do you know that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, of course. Because I adopted the terminology that I was taught during my training. It's only a matter of terminology. We always determined positions from the north. I think Dragan, my colleague, made a mistake here. He could have written 110 degrees from the north. I'm absolutely sure that he made a mistake there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Tapuskovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, Your Honours, what you just asked of both parties is precisely the way you put it. Throughout reports that dealt with similar matters, we come across the same deficiency in the practice of the police and the army in Bosnia-Herzegovina. But let us come back to this problem. I asked for a photograph to be shown, 575, P575.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Can you see it?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: That's the first incident at 1530.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: Probably.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: This arrow shows the direction from which the shell came from?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: That's the probable direction. It's not a perfect photograph because we don't see all the traces. We don't see the other end of the ellipsis of the splash.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Can you explain to me these traces on the right-hand side of the arrow, is that the dispersion of the splinters of the shell? Logically, if the shell came from this direction and the energy of the shell is spread in that direction, how come that all the splinters and fragments of the shell were splashed on one side?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: That's what I was telling you. We don't see but one side. Maybe another photograph. Here we see only one part of the scene. We don't see the traces on the left side, at least not completely.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, please, in the direction from which the shell came from, you don't have a single splinter. Is that visible on the photograph?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: No. I can mark them for you, if you don't see them.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Do splinters have to predominate in the direction from which the shell came from?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: Yes. According to laws of physics, splinters get stuck at the first obstacle. Here, there is no obstacle, and the projectile falls under an angle of 90 degrees, right?

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. How is it possible that this piece of asphalt remains here if that's where the shell came from?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: Which? Which piece?

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: This, this largest piece. This largest chunk that was simply dug out of the asphalt when the shell impacted.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I don't see a single piece that remained. I just see the damage on the pavement.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: If you look at the direction that you drew yourself, you see number 1?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: We see where the remnants of the shell are, and before that you see a large chunk. If the shell came from there, how come this chunk is here?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: On the basis of this photograph, I couldn't tell you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: This damage on the left-hand side, the fragment remaining from the shell. Look at the damage to the pavement.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Isn't this evidence proof as to where the shell came from and the dispersed splinters?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: No. I explained to you how direction of fire is -- is normally established, and this photograph is not a proper basis for determining it. I told the Prosecutor the same thing when he asked me to draw the direction of fire to make this arrow on this photograph. This must be a better photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Apart from this, such fresh traces of an impact show that the distance was not great.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: And how do you know that?

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I will put to the witness, but let us just show him the other shell and the traces. That's photograph 579.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Can you see it?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: Yes. One can see more clearly here.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. But here, again, you mark the dispersed traces on the other side. How is it possible and can you explain it to me that these dispersed traces of shrapnel were behind the from which the shell came, or rather, behind the point of the impact instead of them being dispersed in the direction of the shell?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: But you see that they were dispersed in that way. Only the descent angle was a little bit bigger here. There was dispersion elsewhere but not ought such a great distance from the centre. You can see look at this fan-shape arrangement. Ideally speaking, if it falls under the angle of 90 degrees, then we would have had a perfect ellipsis.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Sabljica, traces of shrapnel, according to your drawings, are all marked as being situated behind the line indicating the source of fire. There is not a single trace that you marked corresponding or parallel to the direction from which the shell was allegedly fired. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: No, it's not. This stick shows the direction from which the shell came. It goes all the way to the centre of the explosion, and it indicates the origin of fire. You see how dispersed the shrapnel are here.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Do I see properly the direction?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: Yes, this is the direction. The direction is marked by this -- by the red arrow, providing that we are looking at the same photograph 6067397, and this vertical stick indicates the direction from which the shell was fired.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Was the shell fired behind the wall, from that direction?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: What? What wall?

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Do you see it?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: No, I don't say it. I see somebody's feet here and I see pavement or I see some grass in the area. I don't know if we will looking at the same photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Sabljica, I see these feet, and I see this wall.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: This is not a wall. This is a pavement, and this is a curb.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Very well, the curb. Did the shell fly over the curb?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: Of course, the curb is ten centimetres high.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: How is it possible then that there were no shrapnel dispersed in the direction from which the shell came and spent its energy and it's power.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: You see, there is. You see all the traces on the curb and the damage inflicted on the curve, and you see how this fan is spreading. Either, I don't understand your question or you don't understand what I'm saying.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: I'm going to shorten this. This is a self-explanatory photograph. All traces of shrapnel are behind these two horizontal sticks. There is not a single shrapnel on the opposite side, and the shell came across the pavement?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: That is not true. What do you think? This is what I marked with the red pen.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: This photograph speaks for itself. I'm asking you: Explain to me why there are no shrapnel on the other side at the bottom of the photograph.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: Because the explosion went upward, and it corresponds to the direction from which the shell came. I think I was clear on that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: This photograph speaks for itself, and all my questions were put to you because I wanted to present to you Defence exhibit DD00-84; English page number 3 and also page number 3 in the B/C/S version. So page 3 in English and also page 3 in B/C/S. And with this I will conclude my cross-examination. I think this will be sufficient, although I could have tackled other issues as well. Mr. Witness, do you see this conclusion?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: It reads as follows, and it all has to do with this last crater: "It is possible to conclude that the most suspected area is under the control of BH. To fire from B/C/S positions for the same range and with the same angle of descent, the direction of the mortar should be 4200 from Grdonj or 700 from Orlovac, which means that the direction of the weapon measured from the impact location should be 1.000 Grdonj or 700 Orlovac." And at the end, it reads as follows: "The impact on the ground are too clear to allow such errors." You answered a minute ago where is it written what I asked you about. This is where it is written. "The impact on the ground are two clear too allow such errors."

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: All this is correct.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This was stated by UNPROFOR experts. And they correspond to the north, north-easterly direction, the one that we could have determined as well. It could have not been otherwise, as you tried to demonstrate to me, that it came from north-west. According to the crater, it is obvious that it came from north-east, and these locations mentioned by UNPROFOR are to the north-east. And based on the traces, it is definite that it came from north-east, whether it came from Grdonj, Orovac, or other locations. They're all to the north-east. If we adopted an approach that you suggest, that it came from north-west, these locations are not there. It is where Vogosca and other locations are there.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: I'm not putting anything categorically to you. It is up to the Chamber to establish beyond a reasonable doubt the origin of fire. What you said is completely contradictory to any logic because craters show that shells came from a different direction. I am not going to investigate this and establish this. I right or am I not right?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: No, are you not. We agreed with UNPROFOR that the shells came from north-east. That's what they said. You read it yourself. They came from north-east, because these places Grdonj, Orovac are on north-east.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: If that is it all, as you say, it says that the most suspected area was under the BH army?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: I don't know about that. It was what they established. I cannot confirm or deny that. Just as I cannot confirm that it was fired from Spicasta Stijena, which is also to the north-east. You know all these locations you are familiar with Sarajevo. And the crater clearly shows the direction was from north-east.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Let me just remind you that they suggest that it was fired from Grdonj under the control of BH army. What do you say to that?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: I cannot say anything to that, just as I cannot claim that it was fired by the VRS positions because I never investigated that aspect.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, this concludes my cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Witness.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Sachdeva.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President, and I will be brief. If we can go to Defence Exhibit 85, please, and I want page -- I believe it's page 8 and 9. Three more pages after this. Next page, please. Sorry. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Witness, you see a document on the screen, and can you just confirm that this is an on-site investigation and analysis of traces from the anti-terrorist division, the KDZ of the Ministry of the Interior?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: Yes, yes. That's correct. This is a KDZ-produced report.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And if we can scroll down to the bottom, please. Actually, on the English it's on this page. We have to go to the next page in the B/C/S. But keep to this page in the English but the next page in the B/C/S, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Okay. On this page, Mr. Sabljica, do you see, towards the bottom, it talks about the angle of descent of the two mortar shells; and then the next paragraph, it reads: "The first shell was fired from a direction north-west to the explosion centre; that is, the first shell that landed at Livanjska Street," and then it talks about the other two shells; do you see that.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: What does it say with respect to the direction of the other two shells?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: You mean the third paragraph? "The first shell was fired from a direction north-west to the explosion centre in the direction of Poljine. The other two shells were fired from a direction north-east of the explosion centre in the direction of Spicasta Stijena-Hladivode."

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: That's the re-examination, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Witness. Before we end, I would just like to return briefly to the question that I put to you earlier on in your testimony; namely, whether it is possible to measure when you have the angle of descent and you have the direction of fire and you know the type of weapon that has been used, the type of mortar, then I asked you whether it was then possible to also determine the geographical distance from which the mortar was fired. And you said, "Yes. It was possible, but that was not done by you but by some experts in the KDZ." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Then my question is: Do you know if such calculations were ever made in the KDZ? I'm asking because we haven't seen many of those, and I cannot recall off the top of my head that we have seen any of those calculations from the KDZ. So my question is: Do you know if they were actually made?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: I think they were because they had on staff people like Emir Turvusic, professors from the university. And I think they prepare this kind of expert reports, particularly in cases of Markale 2, I think there is such a report attached.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Witness that concludes your evidence. We thank you for giving it and you may now leave. We will adjourn until tomorrow. But, Mr. Sachdeva, you have a point.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: One very small point, Mr. President, and I apologise. It is with respect to Prosecution Exhibit 560 from yesterday. I had on the record indicated that pages 31 on a 32 should be admitted; In fact, it should be 31 to 33 of 65 ter --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We'll take a note of that. 31 to 33.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: -- of 65 ter 73. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Isailovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I merely wanted to point out that you asked the Defence to show conclusions, our conclusions to the answer to the request from the Prosecution of April 11, 2007, on the subject of introducing in the 65 ter list of some documents used by the Prosecution, particularly videotapes that might be used with some witnesses. And we, from the Defence, are now in a position to say that we do not oppose this request, because we don't want to -- given that we have overwhelmed with other work, we want to avoid any problems.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We don't want to have it written. We have so much to do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We're adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Friday, the 20th day of April, 2007, at 9.00 a.m.
